section_summary.extract_value: This preliminary analyses section reports that BAS-2 scores had no missing data and other variables had at most 0.5% missingness (Little's MCAR test non-significant). The authors examined normality and found skewness/kurtosis within limits; the two subsamples did not differ significantly in sex, age, or BMI. The section refers to 'both subsamples' but does not provide sample sizes, demographic percentages, or correlations between BAS-2 and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: "There were no missing data in BAS-2 scores. For other variables, maximum of 0.5% items were missing completely at random, Little's MCAR test: -2(886) = 777.55, p = .996. The normality of distribution for all BAS-2 items and total score in both subsamples was examined. Skewness and kurtosis did not exceed the critical limits (Kline, 2010). The two subsamples did not differ significantly in sex, -2(1) = 1.25, p = .295, age, t(717) = −0.53, p = .598, d = 0.04, and BMI, t(716) = 1.42, p = .156, d = 0.11."
